title: Earnings preview: ICICI Bank to post stable NII growth in Q4
summary: Analysts expect ICICI Bank to report stable net interest income growth in Q4FY25, supported by steady loan and deposit expansion. Brokerages project NII of ₹20,865 crore, non-interest income of ₹7,046 crore and net profit of ₹12,070 crore. Key watchpoints include NIM trajectory (around 4.25%) and growth strategy in unsecured loans amid a CASA ratio of 40.5%.
content:
ICICI Bank will likely post stable growth in loans and deposits, aiding nearly double-digit growth in core income in Q4FY25, analysts say. The bank was scheduled to report its Q4 earnings results on April 19, 2025.

Brokerage Motilal Oswal noted the lender has shown sharp resilience, posting a 17 percent CAGR in loans over the FY22-24 period, driven by retail loans, business loans and the small and medium enterprises (SME) segment. The brokerage highlighted the bank's strategic use of data analytics to refine customer onboarding and credit evaluation as a "game-changer" for sustaining momentum.

Deposits at ICICI Bank grew faster than systemic trends, Motilal Oswal said, attributing the outperformance to advanced digital banking capabilities and a robust branch network. However, growth in low-cost deposits has been a challenge: the bank's current and savings account (CASA) ratio stood at 40.5 percent in Q3FY25 amid a high rate environment.

Axis Securities expects net interest margin (NIM) to move with a negative bias, though it sees asset quality remaining stable with lower credit cost. The brokerage projects ICICI Bank's net interest income to grow 9 percent year-on-year in Q4 to ₹20,865 crore, while non-interest income is likely to rise 25 percent year-on-year to about ₹7,046 crore. Axis forecasts the bank's net profit to increase roughly 13 percent year-on-year to ₹12,070 crore in Q4.

Analysts said management commentary on the NIM outlook and the growth strategy for unsecured loans will be key monitorables during the quarter. Motilal Oswal pointed out that NIMs have been under pressure, with current NIMs at about 4.25 percent, down around 18 basis points year-on-year. The pace of decline has tapered, and the bank anticipates near-term stability in margins.

Market watchers will also track deposit mix and the pace of low-cost deposit accretion, given the importance of CASA for margin support. Continued focus on retail and SME lending, coupled with digital onboarding and credit evaluation improvements, remains central to the bank's growth narrative.

Published on April 18, 2025.

The brokerage said ICICI Bank management’s commentary on NIM outlook, along with growth strategy in unsecured loan segment will be the key monitorables during Q4.
